Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue ".NET 11 Release Candidate 1" (#444) at dotnet/announcements
Events.RelatedBody:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

# Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS out-of-process - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.1 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.19 | 9.0.20 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69806 – .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet-watch AspireServerService exposes information through the use of certain arguments, that in turn can enable code injection. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56167 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.0 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor); CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects Linux installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks) on Linux, you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-69806](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-69806) ### Acknowledgements Ky0toFu with Microsoft ### Revisions V1.0 (09/08/2026): Advisory published.

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native can perform an out of bounds write while processing MSFZ PDB files. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/133438 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.10.0-beta1.24272.1, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 10 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 9 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET or Visual Studio. 2. If your application references Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native, update the package reference to version 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 or later. Once you have installed the updated runtime, SDK, Visual Studio, or package, restart your apps for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-58649 – .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet watch BrowserRefreshServer does not adequately validate cross-origin WebSocket origins, potentially allowing IL and PDB information disclosure. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56166 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-346 (Origin Validation Error) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.1xx | >= 9.0.100, <= 9.0.119 | 9.0.120 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ### .NET 8 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 8.0.1xx | >= 8.0.100, <= 8.0.129 | 8.0.130 8.0.4xx | >= 8.0.400, <= 8.0.423 | 8.0.424 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. ### Describe the bug

On Windows, each time the SDK runs with a new `DOTNET_CLI_HOME` (or `HOME`), the first-run experience appends `<home>\.dotnet\tools` to the persistent user PATH (`HKCU\Environment`). There is no deduplication by pattern, no cleanup of directories that no longer exist, and no length check.

Tools that create a fresh, isolated dotnet home per run (CI-like scripts, AI coding agents running test suites in scratch directories) therefore grow the user PATH by one entry per run, indefinitely.

### Observed impact
- User PATH reached roughly 200 entries / ~30,000+ characters, almost all of the form `C:\Users\<user>\...\<run-specific-dir>\dotnet-home\.dotnet\tools` (most of those directories were temporary and no longer exist).
- Once the environment crossed the Windows size limit, the whole user session broke: Start menu and taskbar failed, Task Manager and any elevated process failed with `0xC0000017` (STATUS_NO_MEMORY) despite ~28 GB free RAM, Settings failed with "Class not registered", rundll32 reported "Not enough memory resources". Other user accounts on the same machine were unaffected.
- Trimming `HKCU\Environment\Path` back to its ~10 legitimate entries fixed everything immediately.

### Expected
- Don't persist PATH entries for non-default/temporary homes, or
- deduplicate/prune entries pointing to non-existent directories, and
- never write a PATH value that would exceed the platform limit.

### Workaround
`DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH=false`

### Environment
Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200). The dotnet invocations came from AI coding agents (OpenAI Codex desktop and Anthropic Claude Code) running test suites with a per-run dotnet home; exact SDK version unavailable at the time of writing. I've also reported the agent side to OpenAI and Anthropic.

### Steps to reproduce

_Conceptual repro inferred from the observed PATH contents (not yet verified in isolation):_

```powershell
for ($i = 0; $i -lt 5; $i++) {
  $env:DOTNET_CLI_HOME = "$env:TEMP\dh$i"
  dotnet --info | Out-Null
}
[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path', 'User')   # one new <home>\.dotnet\tools entry per iteration
```

### Expected behavior

The SDK should not persist PATH entries for temporary/non-default dotnet homes, or should deduplicate/prune entries pointing to non-existent directories, and should never write a user PATH that exceeds the platform limit.

### Actual behavior

Each new `DOTNET_CLI_HOME` adds a permanent `<home>\.dotnet\tools` entry to the user PATH (`HKCU\Environment`). After ~200 runs the user PATH exceeded the Windows limit and the user session broke: Start menu/taskbar stopped working, Task Manager and every elevated process failed with `0xC0000017` (STATUS_NO_MEMORY) despite ~28 GB free RAM, Settings failed with "Class not registered", rundll32 reported "Not enough memory resources".

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

### Are there any workarounds?

- Prevent it: set `DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH=false` (user-level env var or in the environment of the tool that invokes dotnet). Reusing a single `DOTNET_CLI_HOME` instead of one per run also avoids the growth.
- Recover a broken session: from another admin account, load the affected user's `NTUSER.DAT` (`reg load`), rewrite `Environment\Path` with only the legitimate entries (as REG_EXPAND_SZ), unload the hive and log back in.

### dotnet --info output

```console

```

### IDE version

_No response_

### Other details

_No response_

After ~200 runs the user PATH exceeded the Windows limit and the user session broke: Start menu/taskbar stopped working, Task Manager and every elevated process failed with `0xC0000017` (STATUS_NO_MEMORY) despite ~28 GB free RAM, Settings failed with "Class not registered", rundll32 reported "Not enough memory resources".

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

### Are there any workarounds?

- Prevent it: set `DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH=false` (user-level env var or in the environment of the tool that invokes dotnet). Reusing a single `DOTNET_CLI_HOME` instead of one per run also avoids the growth.
- Recover a broken session: from another admin account, load the affected user's `NTUSER.DAT` (`reg load`), rewrite `Environment\Path` with only the legitimate entries (as REG_EXPAND_SZ), unload the hive and log back in.

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Fix the language-server publish race
Issues.Body:
This should fix the (intermittent) file locking issue in https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1622972 (and presumably others)

The global `PublishDir` set in `PublishBundledLanguageServer` was redundant, and problematic. The RID-specific value was flowing into project references, creating separate MSBuild project instances that write to the same output paths. The projects being built already calculate the same publish directory through `LanguageServerPublish.props`.

I did a publish before and after the change, For Release, `net10.0`, `win-x64`, and everything in the publish output was identical.

Issues.Title: Avoid quadratic namespace declaration lookup
Issues.Body:
Fixes #85922

Perf results from the issue's benchmark with `concurrentBuild: false`.

Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.9.0:

```text
files  32000 usings per file True :  3.88 s
files  32000 usings per file False:  0.56 s
files  64000 usings per file True : 14.48 s
files  64000 usings per file False:  1.15 s
```

Fixed local Release build:

```text
files  32000 usings per file True : 0.83 s
files  32000 usings per file False: 0.75 s
files  64000 usings per file True : 1.45 s
files  64000 usings per file False: 1.37 s
```

At 64,000 files, the per-file using case drops from 14.48 seconds to 1.45 seconds and scales with the global-using case.

Issues.Title: Collection initialization with `MatchCollection` produces CS0029
Issues.Body:
I don't know if this would be considered a bug, or just something that could be improved. I also haven't looked into whether this is really an issue with Rozlyn or the IDE0305 analyzer. Consider the following code:

```csharp
        Regex re = new ("test pattern");

        Match[] matches = [.. re.Matches("test input").ToList()];    // this compiles and does not suggest simplifying
        Match[] evenMoreMatches = matches.ToArray();             // this compiles but suggests IDE0305 simplifying to the code below
        Match[] moreMatches = [.. re.Matches("test input")];       // this produces CS0029
```

I realize that part of this might be due to classes like `MatchCollection` not being updated to take advantage of collection expressions/initializers. But there's still at least a contradiction between the compiler and analyzer that could be cleared up.

Given that `MatchCollection` implements `IList<Match>`, I would think that the compiler could just easily convert to the fluent form that IDE0305 warns against using explicitly. That is what the first expression compiles to. It just calls `ToList()` first (which also seems like a separate, albeit minor, problem).

Otherwise, the IDE0305 should probably not make the suggestion.

The CS0029 mentions converting `object` to `Match`, so that makes me think that the compiler is trying to use the non-generic `IList` implementation of `MatchCollection`.

Issues.Title: First-run appends <DOTNET_CLI_HOME>\.dotnet\tools to user PATH for every new home dir — unbounded growth breaks Windows logon session
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, each time the SDK runs with a new `DOTNET_CLI_HOME` (or `HOME`), the first-run experience appends `<home>\.dotnet\tools` to the persistent user PATH (`HKCU\Environment`). There is no deduplication by pattern, no cleanup of directories that no longer exist, and no length check.

Tools that create a fresh, isolated dotnet home per run (CI-like scripts, AI coding agents running test suites in scratch directories) therefore grow the user PATH by one entry per run, indefinitely.

### Observed impact
- User PATH reached roughly 200 entries / ~30,000+ characters, almost all of the form `C:\Users\<user>\...\<run-specific-dir>\dotnet-home\.dotnet\tools` (most of those directories were temporary and no longer exist).
- Once the environment crossed the Windows size limit, the whole user session broke: Start menu and taskbar failed, Task Manager and any elevated process failed with `0xC0000017` (STATUS_NO_MEMORY) despite ~28 GB free RAM, Settings failed with "Class not registered", rundll32 reported "Not enough memory resources". Other user accounts on the same machine were unaffected.
- Trimming `HKCU\Environment\Path` back to its ~10 legitimate entries fixed everything immediately.

### Expected
- Don't persist PATH entries for non-default/temporary homes, or
- deduplicate/prune entries pointing to non-existent directories, and
- never write a PATH value that would exceed the platform limit.

### Workaround
`DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH=false`

### Environment
Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200). The dotnet invocations came from AI coding agents (OpenAI Codex desktop and Anthropic Claude Code) running test suites with a per-run dotnet home; exact SDK version unavailable at the time of writing. I've also reported the agent side to OpenAI and Anthropic.

### Steps to reproduce

_Conceptual repro inferred from the observed PATH contents (not yet verified in isolation):_

```powershell
for ($i = 0; $i -lt 5; $i++) {
  $env:DOTNET_CLI_HOME = "$env:TEMP\dh$i"
  dotnet --info | Out-Null
}
[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path', 'User')   # one new <home>\.dotnet\tools entry per iteration
```

### Expected behavior

The SDK should not persist PATH entries for temporary/non-default dotnet homes, or should deduplicate/prune entries pointing to non-existent directories, and should never write a user PATH that exceeds the platform limit.

### Actual behavior

Each new `DOTNET_CLI_HOME` adds a permanent `<home>\.dotnet\tools` entry to the user PATH (`HKCU\Environment`). After ~200 runs the user PATH exceeded the Windows limit and the user session broke: Start menu/taskbar stopped working, Task Manager and every elevated process failed with `0xC0000017` (STATUS_NO_MEMORY) despite ~28 GB free RAM, Settings failed with "Class not registered", rundll32 reported "Not enough memory resources".

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

### Are there any workarounds?

- Prevent it: set `DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH=false` (user-level env var or in the environment of the tool that invokes dotnet). Reusing a single `DOTNET_CLI_HOME` instead of one per run also avoids the growth.
- Recover a broken session: from another admin account, load the affected user's `NTUSER.DAT` (`reg load`), rewrite `Environment\Path` with only the legitimate entries (as REG_EXPAND_SZ), unload the hive and log back in.

### dotnet --info output

```console

```

### IDE version

_No response_

### Other details

_No response_

Issues.Title: Fix the CA1864 title to reference Dictionary.TryAdd
Issues.Body:
Fixes #51141.

The CA1864 title said `Prefer the 'IDictionary.TryAdd(TKey, TValue)' method`, but `IDictionary<TKey, TValue>` doesn't define a `TryAdd` method. The analyzer only reports CA1864 for types that have their own `TryAdd` method (`PreferDictionaryTryMethodsOverContainsKeyGuardAnalyzer` skips types where `GetMembers("TryAdd")` is empty), such as `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>`. The title now says `Prefer the 'Dictionary.TryAdd(TKey, TValue)' method`.

Changes:
- `MicrosoftNetCoreAnalyzersResources.resx`: updated `PreferDictionaryTryAddTitle`.

Issues.Title: Allow the same EmbeddedResource with different LogicalNames
Issues.Body:
Fixes #2657.

Embedding the same file more than once with different `LogicalName` values fails with NETSDK1022, because `CheckForDuplicateItems` groups items only by item spec. Repro on SDK 10.0.401:

```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <EmbeddedResource Include="image.bmp" LogicalName="First.bmp" />
  <EmbeddedResource Include="image.bmp" LogicalName="Second.bmp" />
</ItemGroup>
```

```
error NETSDK1022: Duplicate 'EmbeddedResource' items were included. ... The duplicate items were: 'image.bmp'
```

### Changes
- `CheckForDuplicateItems` has a new optional `DistinguishingMetadataName` parameter. Items with the same item spec are not treated as duplicates when each of them has a different, non-empty value for that metadata. Values are compared ordinally, since manifest resource names are case-sensitive.
- The `EmbeddedResource` check passes `LogicalName`. The `Compile` and `Content` checks are unchanged.
- An item without the metadata still counts as a duplicate. So the case the check exists for (a default-glob item plus an explicit `Include` of the same file) still reports NETSDK1022.
- In design-time builds, `DeduplicatedItems` now keeps all distinct items instead of collapsing them to the first one.

### Tests
4 new tests in `GivenACheckForDuplicateItems`:
- different `LogicalName`s: no error (failed before this change)
- one item without `LogicalName`: still an error
- same `LogicalName`: still an error
- `DeduplicatedItems` keeps the distinct items (failed before this change)

`Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests` locally: 373 passed, 0 failed.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Allow the same EmbeddedResource with different LogicalNames" (#56510)

Issues.Title: Ignore manifest folders without WorkloadManifest.json when merging manifest roots
Issues.Body:
Fixes #21676.

Folders without a `WorkloadManifest.json` are already ignored when there is a single manifest root (`ResolveManifestDirectory`, covered by `GivenNoManifestJsonFileInDirectoryItShouldIgnoreIt`). With multiple roots (user-local install or `DOTNETSDK_WORKLOAD_MANIFEST_ROOTS`), folders were keyed only by name. So an empty leftover folder in a higher-priority root hid a valid manifest with the same ID in a lower-priority root.

This change only records a folder when it contains a manifest, either directly or in a version subfolder.

Tests added:
- `ManifestFolderWithoutManifestInTestHookShouldNotHideDefault` (fails before this change)
- `ManifestInVersionSubfolderOfTestHookShouldOverrideDefault` (guards the subfolder case)

Ran the `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WorkloadManifestReader.Tests` project locally on net472: 114 passed, 1 skipped (`GetPackDefinitionLocations`, already skipped), 0 failed. The net12.0 target builds with no warnings.

Issues.Title: `dotnetup` Perf: Replace .NET Tar with `bsdtar` in Windows
Issues.Body:
We ran some comparisons between `dotnetup`, `Install Scripts`, `apt`, `msi`, and `winget`. In this, we found that `dotnetup` was faster than the `Install Scripts` on my 2 machines, but slower specifically for Windows and .NET 11 installation. It was faster for .NET 10. This led to an investigation.

I identified the issue as .NET Runtime Tar Extraction, vs `tar.exe` or `bsdtar` shipped with Windows. THe .NET Runtime implementation is significantly slower. 

The performance information can be seen here in the issue I filed on the runtime: 
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135128

This PR:
- Adds a small 'native' wrapper which calls the Windows shipped `tar` when available
- Produce the hash of the downloaded content as it's streamed rather than wait for the full file download
- Windows Tar File Count requires double decompression or costly extra work per file with no ideal alternative - for this scenario, install extraction progress is changed to be 'Installing...' with a shimmer; the perf regression was about an additional `1.2-2s` cost to have accurate file count during extraction on Windows. On other platforms, the perf change was minimal `10-80ms` so it was retained if progress is enabled.  
- Prevents work from being done in the progress reporter when `--no-progress` is used
- Prevents hitting `releases-index.json` when all we need to hit is the `major.minor.json`
- Modifies extraction to stage/move directories instead of placing files one at a time to prevent Point-in-Time problems, where the `muxer` might see an sdk as existing even if the file writes did not fully complete (our manifest would not report it but the muxer could still try to use an invalid SDK)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "`dotnetup` Perf: Replace .NET Tar with `bsdtar` in Windows" (#56507)

Issues.Title: Preserve NuGet credential-provider discovery for sudo workload commands
Issues.Body:
On macOS and Linux, `sudo dotnet workload` redirects the CLI home to a temporary directory, so NuGet cannot find credential providers installed in the user’s home. This blocks advertising-manifest updates from authenticated feeds.

- **Provider discovery:** Point NuGet to providers in the original CLI home without copying them. Retain discovery of `PATH`-installed plugins and preserve explicit plugin-path overrides.
- **Home isolation:** Keep writable caches in the temporary home. Ensure the user’s NuGet config can be staged there.
- **Coverage and guidance:** Add focused regression tests and document authenticated-feed behavior under `sudo`.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #35912

Issues.Title: [ResourceLock] Lock workload-resolver opt-out env var across MSBuildSdkResolver tests
Issues.Body:
**Project:** `test/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests` — `MSTestParallelizeScope=ClassLevel` (already parallelized; this PR does not change it).

**Shared resource:** process environment variable `MSBuildEnableWorkloadResolver`.
- Mutators: `GivenACachingWorkloadResolver.WithOptOut` (set/restore in `finally`), used by 5 tests.
- Concurrent observers: `GivenAnMSBuildSdkResolver` tests call `DotNetMSBuildSdkResolver.Resolve`, which constructs `CachingWorkloadResolver` and calls `IsEnabled()`, reading that variable (`src/Resolvers/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WorkloadMSBuildSdkResolver/CachingWorkloadResolver.cs`). Under ClassLevel parallelism a resolve test could observe `false` and skip workload resolution.

**Change:** `[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.EnvironmentVariables)]` on the 5 env-mutating methods only (the other tests in that class do not touch the variable), and on `GivenAnMSBuildSdkResolver` at class level since every `Resolve` call there samples the variable. Previous values were already restored exactly in `finally`.

**Validation**
- `./.dotnet/dotnet build test/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests.csproj` — succeeded, 0 warnings / 0 errors.
- `./.dotnet/dotnet scripts/RunTests.cs -- --skip-redist-check --project test/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests/Microsoft.DotNet.MSBuildSdkResolver.Tests.csproj` — **not run to completion**: the project targets only `net472`, and the runner reports it "can only run on Windows". `--framework net11.0` fails with NETSDK1005. Tests were not executed on this Linux runner.

Issues.Title: [ResourceLock] Use ResourceLock instead of DoNotParallelize in NuGetPackageDownloaderFactoryTests
Issues.Body:
Replaces `[DoNotParallelize]` with a method-level `[ResourceLock(WellKnownResources.EnvironmentVariables)]` in `Microsoft.DotNet.PackageInstall.Tests`, and adds the matching lock to the one test that observes the same variable.

**Project / scope:** `test/Microsoft.DotNet.PackageInstall.Tests`, `MSTestParallelizeScope=ClassLevel`.

**Shared resource and conflicting tests:** `DOTNET_NUGET_SIGNATURE_VERIFICATION`. The `NuGetPackageDownloader` constructor reads it when `verifySignatures` is true (`src/Cli/dotnet/NugetPackageDownloader/NuGetPackageDownloader.cs`).
- `Constructor_WhenVerifyRequestedButPlatformUnsupported_LogsMessage` mutates it (restored in `finally`).
- `CreateForWorkloads_WithAllParameters_ReturnsConfiguredDownloader` passes `verifyNuGetSignatures: true`, so it reads it. It now takes the same lock.
- Other constructions in the project pass `verifySignatures: false`, which short-circuits before the read, so they need no lock.

**Why minimal:** the variable lives in this assembly, so the in-assembly lock covers both the mutator and the observer. Both locks are method-level; the rest of the class stays fully parallel.

**Validation:**
- `.dotnet/dotnet msbuild test/Microsoft.DotNet.PackageInstall.Tests/Microsoft.DotNet.PackageInstall.Tests.csproj -restore` — succeeded.
- Focused run, `.dotnet/dotnet exec Microsoft.DotNet.PackageInstall.Tests.dll --filter "ClassName~NuGetPackageDownloaderFactoryTests"` — not validated. All 4 tests failed in the `SdkTest` constructor (`SdkTestContext`/`ToolsetInfo.Create`). The runner has no built redist SDK layout, and I did not run a full `build.sh`. The failure is unrelated to this change.

`MSTestParallelizeScope` is unchanged.

Issues.Title: DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en-US does not affect C# compiler diagnostics for file-based apps
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: 
.NET SDK: 10.0.401
OS: Windows 10 x64

**Steps to Reproduce**:

1. Create project.cs:
```
Console.WriteLine("Hello");

if (false)
{
    Console.WriteLine("This produces CS0162");
}
```
2. Set the environment variable:
```
$env:DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE = "en-US"
```
3. Verify:
```
$env:DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE
dotnet --version
```
```
en-US
10.0.401
```
4. Run:
```
dotnet run .\project.cs -- r
```
5. The compiler produces localized diagnostic based on OS language (warning CS0162).


**Expected Behavior**:
With DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en-US, I would expect the compiler diagnostic to be displayed in English:
```
warning CS0162: Unreachable code detected
```

**Additional Observation**:
The compiler diagnostic language can be changed by adding this to the source file:
```
#:property PreferredUILang=en-US
```

This suggests that DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE is not being propagated to the C# compiler's PreferredUILang setting when compiling a file-based app.

Is this expected behavior for file-based apps, or should DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en-US also control the language of C# compiler diagnostics?

If it is expected behavior, is there a supported way to globally configure the C# compiler diagnostic language for file-based apps without adding #:property PreferredUILang=en-US to every source file?

I would like to add that it looks like removing ```#:property PreferredUILang=en-US``` from source file does not revert localization back to OS language.

Issues.Title: Normalize package pseudo-locale satellite casing consistently
Issues.Body:
🤖 Windows NLS and ICU disagree on the casing of pseudo-locale names, leaving package satellite output directories and NETSDK1187 diagnostics dependent on the build host. This addresses the remaining casing issue in #53815 while preserving the culture-remapping protection introduced by merged PR #53817.

## Approach

- Recognize only `qps-ploc`, `qps-plocm`, and `qps-ploca`, case-insensitively, and use lowercase output culture/destination metadata without casing diagnostics.
- Preserve original package paths, satellite assembly culture metadata, and embedded resource names. Ordinary corrections such as `ru-ru` to `ru-RU` and the protection against NLS remapping `ckb` to `ku` remain unchanged.
- Increment the asset cache version so existing caches cannot retain the old normalization results.
- Add regressions for casing variants, language filtering, warm/old caches, build/publish output, `.deps.json`, unchanged satellite bytes/metadata, and actual NLS/ICU resource loading without parent fallback.

## Validation

- Repository build succeeded.
- ResolvePackageAssets task tests: 61 passed.
- Satellite culture integration tests: 18 passed, including the existing Kurdish regressions.
- Focused ILLink publishing tests: 4 passed.
- Prior compatibility investigation also verified Linux ICU loading on a case-sensitive filesystem using SDK 10.0.401/runtime 10.0.12. The patched SDK regression run was on Windows; macOS was not executed.

Fixes #53815

Issues.Title: Expand optimized publish to conservative trimmed app scenarios
Issues.Body:
🤖 Extend `UseOptimizedPublish` beyond Native AOT so eligible trimmed applications avoid a redundant root-project build deployment while still compiling. This is the first conservative .NET 12 rollout, not a general replacement for Build during publish.

## Approach

- Default to optimized publish for plain trimmed, self-contained C# executables targeting net11+ on an explicit desktop/server RID allowlist. Eligibility is separate from the public switch, so explicit `true` cannot force unsupported scenarios.
- Keep combined single-file/ReadyToRun modes, specialized SDKs/workloads, native-interoperability scenarios, and older TFMs outside the new expansion. Existing Native AOT eligibility remains unchanged.
- Generate managed runtime configuration under the intermediate publish directory using shared runtime-setting preparation, without rebasing public build paths. Collect XML documentation from compiler output and keep dependency metadata publish-owned.
- Preserve `UseOptimizedPublish=false`, the separate NoBuild route, explicit Build, and normal project-reference builds. Register the intermediate runtime configuration for Clean without priming Build's incremental-clean snapshot or enrolling the published deployment in its ownership.

The TFM policy deliberately includes net11 projects using SDK 12; it is not net12-only. Build-hook integrations that need runnable `bin` output must opt out until adapted. The documentation describes this behavior change and OpenAPI/XML serializer coordination limitations.

## Validation

- Redist build succeeded with zero warnings or errors.
- 52 focused trimmed-publish/ILLink cases passed, covering runnable trimmed output, resources/content, opt-out, unsupported eligibility, NoBuild, repeated publish, custom paths, Build/Publish ordering, and Clean behavior.
- Four existing Native AOT and unsupported-mode controls passed, including executable project-reference coverage.
- No skipped cases. Local execution was Windows x64; other allowlisted platforms still require CI validation.

Related to #55911; this implements only the first rollout step.

Includes incremental single-platform archive reuse, the opt-out property, cached task outputs, archive integrity verification, atomic archive replacement, timestamp validation, and the source regression tests and resource updates.

> This issue is a locked mirror of dotnet/core/discussions/10480. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Preview 7. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/preview7).

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/dotnetmaui.md)

- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/preview7/libraries.md)

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-62900 | .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git and Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Improper removal of sensitive information before storage or transfer in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sourcelink/issues/1757 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-212: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### Published NuGet packages Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 The affected packages used by .NET 8 and .NET 9 SDKs are built with SDK-specific prerelease versions that aren't published as stable NuGet packages. Update to SDK 8.0.130 or 8.0.424, SDK 9.0.120 or 9.0.317, or SDK 10.0.111 or 10.0.303 to receive the fix. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-50648 | .NET Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET XML Encryption (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. A denial of service vulnerability exists in the XML encryption implementation (EncryptedXml) in .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted encrypted XML that causes uncontrolled resource consumption, resulting in denial of service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/130714 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.3 | 8.0.4 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? To update the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml NuGet package, use one of the following methods: NuGet Package Manager UI in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Right-click on your project in Solution Explorer and select "Manage NuGet Packages..." or navigate to "Project > Manage NuGet Packages". - In the NuGet Package Manager window, select the "Updates" tab. This tab lists packages with available updates from your configured package sources. - Select the package(s) you wish to update. You can choose a specific version from the dropdown or update to the latest available version. - Click the "Update" button. Using the NuGet Package Manager Console in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Navigate to "Tools > NuGet Package Manager > Package Manager Console". - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following Update-Package command: ```Update-Package -Id System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Using the .NET CLI (Command Line Interface): - Open a terminal or command prompt in your project's directory. - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following add package command: ```dotnet add package System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Once you have updated the nuget package reference you must recompile and deploy your application. Additionally we recommend you update your runtime and/or SDKs, but it is not necessary to patch the vulnerability. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-50527 | .NET Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET XML Encryption (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. A denial of service vulnerability exists in the XML encryption implementation (EncryptedXml) in .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted encrypted XML that is improperly validated, resulting in denial of service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/130712 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-121 (Stack-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.3 | 8.0.4 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? To update the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml NuGet package, use one of the following methods: NuGet Package Manager UI in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Right-click on your project in Solution Explorer and select "Manage NuGet Packages..." or navigate to "Project > Manage NuGet Packages". - In the NuGet Package Manager window, select the "Updates" tab. This tab lists packages with available updates from your configured package sources. - Select the package(s) you wish to update. You can choose a specific version from the dropdown or update to the latest available version. - Click the "Update" button. Using the NuGet Package Manager Console in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Navigate to "Tools > NuGet Package Manager > Package Manager Console". - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following Update-Package command: ```Update-Package -Id System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Using the .NET CLI (Command Line Interface): - Open a terminal or command prompt in your project's directory. - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following add package command: ```dotnet add package System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Once you have updated the nuget package reference you must recompile and deploy your application. Additionally we recommend you update your runtime and/or SDKs, but it is not necessary to patch the vulnerability. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new).
